question.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\sqrt{6t},\,3,\,-t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{6t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{\sqrt{6t}},\,0,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\sqrt{6t},\,3,\,-t⟩\cdot ⟨\frac{3}{\sqrt{6t}},\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =t+3, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{6t})}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}+{(-t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}+6t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{(t+3)^{2}} \\  & =t+3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{t+3}{t+3} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
